text:
Jules (product): quick q — where should saved queries live in Console? put them in the filter shelf inline, or a separate ‘Query Library’? thinking about per-route vs per-model scope and discoverability. cc @Maria Chen
Maria Chen (eng): i vote library. shelf is fine for pins, but long-term we need metadata (owner, scope, telemetry impact) that clutters the shelf.
Ben Park (design): Library + smart shelf. shelf shows pinned & recent, library for management/search. keeps main UI clean. can we surface "most-used" per-route?
Jules (product): yep, that’s the tension — pins vs global queries. we also need to be careful about telemetry & quota attribution if people reuse queries across routes.
Raj Patel (platform): telemetry attribution is the big one. if a saved query is executed on multiple routes, do we attach telemetry to the query id or to the route? both matter for rollouts.
Casey Ng (data): attach to route primarily, but keep query-level counters for usage & regressions. we should emit both: route_query_executions and query_agg_executions. sampling/resolution can differ.
Anna Rivera (growth): from a product POV discovery matters. folks expect autosuggest when they open the shelf: type -> show matching saved queries (owned, org-shared). also need permission/filtering UX.
Ben Park (design): rough promo layout idea:
```
[Filter shelf]
 - pinned query A (route-scoped)
 - pinned query B (model-scoped)
 [Query Library (modal)]
 - list view: name | scope | owner | last-run | shared
 - detail pane: preview, telemetry sparkline, apply button
```
Maria Chen (eng): API-wise we should keep the saved-query contract tiny. propose:
```
{
  "id":"q_123",
  "name":"Errors by model",
  "scope":"route|model",
  "owner":"team-a",
  "shared":true,
  "telemetry_sample":0.1
}
```
Raj Patel (platform): +1 on small contract. Important: include `compatibility` field listing which console routes or model-types query works with — helps UI disable apply button when incompatible.
Jules (product): good call. also need ownership/transfer flow (team handover).
Casey Ng (data): small ask: when someone saves a query, store a canonical prompt/hash so we can backfill quality/regression alerts tied to that query. otherwise saved queries are opaque.
Maria Chen (eng): doable. store `fingerprint` (sha256) and sample of last N results. privacy caveats for embeddings/outputs though.
Ben Park (design): on the shelf, what about a compact pill with an ellipsis menu for quick actions: run, duplicate, pin, share, inspect telemetry. keeps clicks low. :thumbsup:
Jules (product): action items:
 - Maria/Raj: design API fields incl. compatibility + fingerprint (owner: eng)
 - Ben: mock shelf + library flows (owner: design)
 - Casey: telemetry naming & counters (owner: data)
 - Anna: copy/visibility requirements + sharing defaults (owner: growth)
I’ll sync with infra for quota implications (if a saved query is scheduled or auto-run).
deploy-bot: scheduled deployment to staging succeeded — console-query-prefs v0.2.3.
Anna Rivera (growth): one more ask — expose simple embed link for saved queries so teams can share in docs. low friction.
Maria Chen (eng): love that. add `share_link` nullable to the contract.
Jules (product): cool. if nobody objects we’ll prototype library + smart shelf approach for the next sprint and add telemetry contract to the evals checklist.
Ben Park (design): no objections. will drop mocks by EOD Monday.
Raj Patel (platform): flag: if we let agents auto-run saved queries we might need rate-limiting sch/quotas. will follow-up with proposal.
Jules (product): noted — follow-up thread for quotas/auto-run. thanks all :rocket:
